name: Meir Kahane
role: Rabbi, founder of the Jewish Defense League and Kach, and member of the Knesset (1984–1988)
summary: Meir Kahane advocated a Jewish state governed by Jewish religious law, open to Jewish immigration and committed to annexing the territories Israel captured in 1967. He proposed removing Arab residents and introduced legislation to deny non-Jews citizenship and prohibit intermarriage. His economic program favored private enterprise and removing barriers to investment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he argues that ending the bureaucracy’s control and relying on free enterprise are necessary for Israel to prosper.

property-fundamental.rationale: Kahane’s proposed expulsion program in “Separation – Only Separation” expressly provides for withholding compensation for property from people forcibly expelled after refusing to leave.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources reviewed do not establish a position on the full statement.

state-harmful.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he gives the proposed Jewish state duties in education, defense, and the public observance of religion.

abortion-legal.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he would permit abortion only when the mother is in danger.

more-religion-public.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he requires religious education and public observance of the Sabbath and Jewish dietary rules.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he makes transmitting Jewish religion and identity a central purpose of education.

nation-first.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he treats preserving a Jewish state as a priority even when pursuing peace would call for concessions.

open-borders.rationale: In “The Answer,” he says the state must limit the number of noncitizen residents it allows to remain.

democracy-best.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill that would limit citizenship to Jews and remove the rights of non-Jews to vote or hold public office.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The federal court recorded Kahane’s 1971 guilty plea and found that he later tried to organize politically motivated attacks on foreign embassies.

separate-church-state.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he makes the government responsible for teaching Judaism and enforcing the public observance of Jewish law.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he sets out public laws grounded in Torah and gives Jewish religious law authority over issues including abortion.

ethnic-nation.rationale: In “The Answer,” he describes Israel as the state of the Jewish people and makes maintaining a Jewish majority a requirement.

harm-principle.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he proposes legal restrictions on consensual relationships and public Sabbath observance on religious grounds.

conscription.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he would use the second and third years of compulsory military service to teach and practice a trade.

territorial-expansion.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for annexing all the territories Israel captured in 1967.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he describes the Land of Israel as the home of the Jewish people and the state as their political representative.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: In “The Answer,” he maintains that Jews from abroad may settle in Israel and acquire citizenship as members of the Jewish nation.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In “Separation – Only Separation,” Kahane proposes reserving national insurance payments for Jews and denying noncitizen residents benefits reserved for citizens.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill requiring separate beaches for Jews and non-Jews and requiring approval from Jewish residents for non-Jews to move into a Jewish neighborhood.

night-watchman-state.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he assigns government responsibility for the religious and cultural education of young people.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kahane submitted a citizenship bill that would deny non-Jews political rights and bar them from residing within the municipal boundaries of Jerusalem.

restrict-conversion.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for prohibiting missionary proselytizing and closing missionary centers while allowing non-Jewish worship.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he says all public schools should teach Judaism and sets a religious instruction minimum for private schools as well.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he holds that the Torah binds the Jewish state even when most voters reject its authority.

population-transfer.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill to remove non-Jews who refused to accept the proposed new resident status, including through compulsory expulsion.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: The federal court found that Kahane tried to organize attacks on foreign embassies in response to violence against Israelis elsewhere.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he proposes restricting movies and theater to protect the religious and moral character of Jewish audiences.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he proposes preventing newsstands from selling pornography, without exempting sales to adults for private use.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he rejects trading territory for peace because he believes Jews have a religious obligation to retain the Land of Israel.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls areas captured in 1967 liberated territory and asserts Jewish title and the right to annex them without the consent of their Palestinian residents.

refugee-return.rationale: In “The Answer,” Kahane explicitly rejects the return of the Arab refugees who fled in 1948.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he urges diaspora Jews to leave for Israel and treats ending the Jewish diaspora as a religious imperative.

patriotic-education.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he would make restoring pride in Jewish identity and teaching attachment to the Land of Israel central tasks of the public schools.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for Israel to sustain itself through work, production and exports instead of relying on foreign financial support.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he rejects Western democracy as a governing ideal for a Jewish state and bases his program on Torah.

religious-nation.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he defines Jewish membership by birth to a Jewish mother or conversion under Jewish religious law.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he regards domestic capitalism as essential to the economic foundation of the society he proposes.

historical-land-claim.rationale: In “The Answer,” Kahane asserts Jewish title to the Land of Israel and rejects Palestinian claims to sovereignty there.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he discusses Auschwitz and demands German reparations for property taken from Jews during the Holocaust.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he says that God gave Jews the laws that establish and direct their state and government.

social-market-economy.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he advocates an economy based on free enterprise. In “Separation – Only Separation,” he retains public welfare and national insurance, with eligibility restricted by national membership.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” Kahane retains a standing military and assigns it responsibility for defending Jews abroad.

racial-franchise.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill that confined citizenship to members of the Jewish people and barred non-Jewish residents from voting in elections to any public body.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill prohibiting Jewish residents from marrying non-Jews and requiring existing interfaith couples to separate.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he gives public schools a duty to raise young Jews in their religious faith.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Kahane’s citizenship bill barred non-Jews from holding positions of public authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Kahane’s citizenship bill barred non-Jewish residents from voting for any public body.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The sources reviewed do not establish a position on the full statement.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for the voluntary mass migration of Jews to Israel and describes the end of diaspora life as a religious duty.

family-wage.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for fair manual wages sufficient for workers to support their families.

spiritual-nature.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he says the government’s first concern should be restoring the spiritual identity of Jewish youth.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he proposes using Israeli forces abroad to protect Jewish people who are neither Israeli citizens nor residents.

communal-electorates.rationale: Kahane’s citizenship bill excluded non-Jews from elections to the Knesset and other public bodies.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: In the discussion of self-defense in Never Again!, Kahane advocates weapons training for young civilians to protect Jewish neighborhoods.

sacred-nation.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls the Jewish state a sanctification of God and describes preserving future generations of Jews as a sacred obligation.

religions-one-truth.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he takes Israel’s existence as proof of the truth of Judaism and sets it in opposition to Christianity and Islam.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he says that only conversion under the interpretation of Jewish law he recognizes should be valid for legal identification as Jewish.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he treats the whole Torah as the exact word of God and grounds moral judgment in it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: In “The Answer,” he rejects any national sovereignty for non-Jews in the land and leaves them only personal rights as residents.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he calls for annexation of the territories captured in 1967 as an obligation arising from Jewish title to the land.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he says the land belongs to God, who gave it to the Jewish people.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he assigns Israel responsibility for defending Jewish communities abroad, including those in neighboring countries.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he gives government a duty to promote religious education and the public observance of Jewish law.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: In “Separation – Only Separation,” he encourages Arab residents, including people who held Israeli citizenship at the time, to leave for Arab countries or elsewhere.

four-day-week.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he explicitly proposes a five-day working week.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: In “Separation – Only Separation,” he calls for removal of most Arabs, while proposing that a limited number be allowed to stay as noncitizen residents.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Kahane submitted a bill canceling government programs intended to bring Jews and Arabs into contact and providing for segregated public spaces.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The federal court found that Kahane had pursued political aims through criminal acts, including trying to induce attacks on foreign embassies.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: The sources reviewed do not establish a position on the full statement.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: In “A Jewish State,” he proposes an economy based on private factories employing workers and calls for manual workers to earn family-supporting wages.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: The federal court found that Kahane tried to induce others to carry out attacks on foreign embassies in response to violence against Israelis.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The sources reviewed do not establish a position on the full statement.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: In “The Answer,” he pairs the right of Jews abroad to settle automatically with strict limits on admission of non-Jews.

notes: Reviewed Kahane’s books on economics, welfare, civil liberties, religion, culture, government, foreign relations and political means. Searched their text for issues in technology and ecology. Checked the Knesset corpus by member ID, which covers recorded plenum votes from 2003, after his term. Project Gutenberg returned no works under his name.
